items.name: Nekton
items.description: Newest raider robot in the game, with an overall strength level pretty comparable to Vulcan. Has incredibly high uptime flight, but isn’t so over the top as other current releases in the meta. In order to counter it, you must use shieldbreaker AND high defense penetration, as just having one of these without the other won’t be enough.

items.name: ⬆️Fang
items.description: Fang is the most recent development in gamebreaking saboteurs. Aside from its insane speed, it applies a powerful EMP and rust effect (through walls!) and has weirdly high firepower for a saboteur. As it exits stealth upon firing, the pilot grants it a durable aegis shield to give itself some cover, and the fact that it has multiple charges of its ability allows it to quickly reenter stealth after unloading. ⬆️Since Fang can quickly enter/exit stealth, it can choose to come out only after Iaraghi has fired. Additionally, its ability to EMP through stasis barrier makes it one of the only real counters to the Iaraghi UE Raven.

items.name: Pathfinder
items.description: The oldest and most f2p friendly X tier bot, Pathfinder hunter stacks are extremely busted and can turn f2p bots into titans and whale titans into unstoppable nightmares.

items.name: Shoggoth
items.description: A more lethal but less tanky version of pathfinder with the same broken mark ability.

items.name: ⬇️Vulcan
items.description: A walking nuclear amplifier. When scaled up, this robot is difficult to take down without some way of ignoring its powerful forcefield, and it has absurd firepower. ⬇️Vulcan’s powerful forcefield is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Omen Vulcan
items.description: The special edition Omen version of Vulcan is noticeably more powerful than the regular edition due to its synergy with the Webby drone, allowing permanent application of 100% rust effect. It’s the first special edition to warrant its own entry on the tier list simply because future tier lists will need to differentiate between the Vulcans. While both currently occupy the top tier, if it gets nerfed, there’s a chance that the special edition one will be a tier above the regular so long as it retains the Webby synergy. ⬇️Vulcan’s powerful forcefield is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬆️UE Rhino
items.description: Currently the tankiest among the UE bots, though it suffers due to the fact that 90% of the time, it only has access to a pair of light weapons (Stalker firepower in the big 26?). Still, it is nigh impossible to kill while in ability and extremely fast to boot. ⬆️Rhino is both tanky enough to occasionally survive shots from Iaraghi (especially when DoT conversion is up) and it has a reliable physical shield.

items.name: ⬇️UE Hawk
items.description: Susceptible to chip damage and lacks deft survivor, but otherwise an incredibly powerful bot with a very strong built in weapon, the strongest reflector in the game, and insane ability uptime. ⬇️Iaraghi completely ignores reflectors, making UE Hawk incredibly easy to instakill when it flies up.

items.name: ⬆️UE Raven
items.description: Unsurprisingly an insanely powerful and sustainable robot thanks to its original counterpart having aged so well already. Immense damage paired with the best defense system in the game as well as the option to go with limitless gray healing if the user chooses to. Only real counters against UE Raven are EMP & Lockdown, as UE Raven isn’t able to jump while locked down. Otherwise, the single strongest duelist robot in X tier and it’s not even close. ⬆️UE Raven is both resilient to Iaraghi thanks to stasis barrier as well as a great platform for Iaraghi. It can even jump to get an angle over most physical shields, removing one of the few counters to Iaraghi. The full build is so unreasonably broken that it can beat most hackers.

items.name: UE Typhon
items.description: Top tier endgame option, able to shut down titans in a way nothing else can perfectly replicate.

items.name: UE Scorpion
items.description: Largely in this tier due to the fact that it’s one of few ways to effectively counter Anaksor. Teleporting to them when they land can yield a quick kill if they don’t respect your range. UE Scorpion has all-around strong stats, however, making it the next most powerful saboteur/assassin in the game after Fang.

items.name: UE Loki
items.description: A mostly worse Fang in terms of assassinations and beacon running, but has an extremely powerful ability of executing robots (and titans!) each time the UE Loki exits stealth. You can think of UE Loki as more or less a hybrid of a Fang meeting a Lynx, while also being able to abuse the same meta grade equipment that you’d put on either of the other robots.

items.name: ⬆️UE Revenant
items.description: Both a cracked opener and an incredible tank. This robot combines extreme sustain and mobility into a single OP package. Most X tier opener bots are on approximately the same level, but this is a personal favorite of Adazahi. ⬆️UE Revenant’s unbreakable side shields can provide it with some protection from Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Nuo
items.description: Powerful support with a buff that’s similar to Pathfinder’s, trading permanent uptime after acquisition for a more frontloaded buff that doesn’t require a kill. Also gives blind stacks, grey immunity and healing, but enemies will often track it down and prioritize killing it. Additionally, Nuo’s high damage and speed make it a fairly strong sniper with wide target access. ⬇️While Nuo is a good platform for Iaraghi, its only form of defense (counterblind) is triggers only after it has already been instakilled by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Dedopali
items.description: Dedopali combines Newton’s lift, strong offensive autonomous turrets, blinding utility, and a passive invisibility defense system into a single unique support bot. While it won’t be conducting spawn raids on its own, it will be able to completely shut down maps from titans trying to advance onto beacons, giving it a unique place on the team as an endgame control bot. That being said, its performance in practice can be far more unreliable than its performance in theory, as the gravity lift rocket is fairly inconsistent. ⬇️Ironically, Dedopali is a victim of its own weapons, as it can get instakilled before the cloak triggers.

items.name: Ammit
items.description: One of the slowest robots in the game but as well as one of the tankiest, able to abuse both Showdown’s healing and innate powerful gray damage resistance. Jump unit is strongly advised, and Ammit has mostly been turned into a beacon rush exclusive robot.

items.name: UE Lancelot
items.description: While Lance has a lot of sustain through its grey healing, the nerf it got to its HP was very significant and made it susceptible to being bursted down. Still, it is an incredibly strong tank nonetheless.

items.name: ⬆️UE Shell
items.description: Mostly a sidegrade to UE Lancelot, having the same issue of charging nuclear amplifiers but is otherwise still quite a functional and powerful beacon contester. The blastwave’s knockback is extremely strong against enemy new gen robots. ⬆️UE Shell’s shields are incredible defense against Iaraghi.

items.name: UE Haechi
items.description: Functional as both a solid opener and a mid to late game Titan slayer. Oppressively annoying to beat without shieldbreaker, but relatively easy to beat with it.

items.name: ⬇️UE Leo
items.description: Fairly tanky attacker with all around solid stats. Has the ability to easily stack both QR and SB together via the pilot and Hawkeye drone, while still having room for Phase Shift, Advanced Repair, or UC. Unfortunately, it’s a bit susceptible to chip damage, and some high damage builds may be able to kill it through the reflector. ⬇️UE Leo’s reflector is ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬆️UE Ravana
items.description: Considering Ravana itself has always been serviceable, it’s no surprise that the ultimate version is exceptionally strong. Transcendance/Phase Shift are just really powerful abilities. ⬆️If you have good reflexes, Ravana can be an incredibly difficult bot for Iaraghi builds to kill.who

items.name: ⬇️UE Fenrir
items.description: A top tier tank, similar to Ammit, but slightly worse, as it doesn’t have the whole built in weapon and insane uptime purple shield. Can become nearly immortal with certain support robots helping it however, like a Nuo/Lio link. ⬇️Fenrir’s DMI and resistance is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: UE SWORD
items.description: While UE Sword doesn’t tickle quite like regular Sword, it will be much rarer than it was before to get charged up enough to actually do hugely significant damage with the slashes. When it does happen, however, it can be match-deciding.

items.name: ⬇️Lio
items.description: Extremely competent support bot with the potential to turn a teammate into an incredibly hard to kill tank. That being said, it’s as susceptible to being hunted down and killed just as Nuo is, and the defense it provides is often not as valuable as Nuo’s offense. In the past, it was a pretty good tank itself with Showdown, but nowadays, you’d rather not expose yourself if you can avoid it. ⬇️Lio’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Imugi
items.description: Powerful Skirmisher and beacon capper with great uptime. Webby synergy allows it to support the team by debuffing enemies during fly-bys. Just hope the enemy isn’t using QR or seeker.

items.name: ⬇️Vector
items.description: Vector’s initial nerf was already enough to demote it from X to S, but with the most recent rebalance, it’s now gone from S to A. While still a better aged brawler, and still capable of throwing people with the vortex, it’s weirdly slower than a jump unit Ammit, which is saying something on the mobility front. Mostly another beacon rush exclusive robot now. ⬇️Vector’s reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Demeter
items.description: A valuable support that can rescue friendly bots from the most perilous of situations. Strongest during titan phase, but weak to shieldbreaker titans such as Bersagliere.

items.name: ⬇️Anaksor
items.description: A more modern but still unfortunately overnerfed raider. Long ability duration doesn’t matter much as you’re only protected for roughly 6 seconds total through invisibility, which means you very often have to land early. Damage potential wise however, Anaksor hasn’t changed much, so it at least has that still going for it. ⬇️Similarly to Dedopali, Anaksor can be instakilled before the cloak triggers.

items.name: Bagliore
items.description: Some of the highest firepower possible in the game with a useful teleport, strong heal, and some defense points. Great sniper platform.

items.name: Stryx
items.description: Similar to Bagliore, a really powerful sniper platform with high damage potential and built in shieldbreaker. Lacks the groundwork damage boost that Bagliore has but makes up for it by wielding 5 heavies. That being said, it does spend a substantial amount of time with only 3 heavies available.

items.name: ⬆️Crisis
items.description: Trades off the tankiness of Stryx and Bagliore for permanent stealth. Has built in shieldbreaker like Stryx and a damage boost like Bagliore, but 4 heavies without nearly as big a damage boost as Bagliore. ⬆️Crisis is a pretty good Iaraghi platform as it can stay cloaked and come out only when it's safe to fire. Unfortunately, most Iaraghi builds can instakill Crisis by blind firing it due to the large hitbox.

items.name: Dux
items.description: The drones pack a punch and can ignore defense points - a rare and powerful feature that makes for a good anti-tank bot. Webby synergy allows it to prevent healing, leaning even further into its anti-tank role. A personal favorite of Spiritings.

items.name: Kaji
items.description: A unique robot that can set relatively dangerous traps. Limited range on the mines prevents its niche from being represented in higher tiers, however.

items.name: ⬆️Hastatus
items.description: Solid mid-late game bot that can poke titans and tanks pretty much for free, but requires reliable cover to function properly and can’t stall for nearly as long as it could before its nerf. ⬆️Stasis barrier charges are very annoying to deplete when running an Iaraghi build.

items.name: ⬆️Rex
items.description: Capable of outputting a ton of damage, but susceptible to being bursted down due to its significantly nerfed resistance. Needs to be played more like a saboteur and less like a brawler. ⬆️Rex’s DoT cleansing makes it immune to Iaraghi while in ability.

items.name: ⬇️Raptor
items.description: Solid opener robot. It can be a competent disruptor with EMP from the pilot. Superjump with jump unit allows it to be first to center on many maps, and its massive grey resist makes it benefit greatly from showdown. ⬇️Raptor’s reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️UE Phantom
items.description: Really fast and relatively tanky with good sustain, but not as tanky as modern tanks, who can often feel comparable (albeit still ultimately worse) in terms of mobility. Nonetheless an acceptable opener bot. ⬇️UE Phantom’s DMI and resistance is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: UE Blitz
items.description: Great stats all around with solid damage potential, a nigh unbreakable shield, and strong suppression, but similarly to Haechi, fails when faced with shieldbreaker.

items.name: ⬆️UE Bulgasari
items.description: If used properly, the unbreakable shield and dashes give it great stalling potential. Unfortunately it’s completely eaten alive by splash damage. ⬆️UE Bulgasari’s unbreakable physical shield can provide some protection against Iaraghi.

items.name: UE Rayker
items.description: Kind of like a downgraded pathfinder, able to abuse Freezo and harass enemies with suppression that actually does great damage and can even execute. Unfortunately, it lacks the mark ability that keeps pathfinder solidly in X tier.

items.name: UE Ao Jun
items.description: Competent titan slayer, but not nearly on the level of UE Hawk.

items.name: UE Spectre
items.description: Very high damage potential with stealth and 4 medium slots.

items.name: UE Ares
items.description: Inverted UE Spectre, high damage potential with absorber and 4 medium slots.

items.name: ⬇️UE Leech
items.description: High damage potential with damage resistance and 4 medium slots. ⬇️UE Leech’s DMI and defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️UE Griffin
items.description: Starting to see a pattern yet? High damage potential with blind and 4 medium slots. ⬇️UE Griffin’s counterblind triggers only after it gets onetapped by Iaraghi.

items.name: ‼️Lynx
items.description: Competent tank-buster thanks to its high uptime stealth, forcefield, and the strongest execution in the game. ‼️For the duration of the Harmattan shotgun meta, Lynx can perform at an X tier level due to how quickly it can defeat just about any target with its execution combined with percentage damage shotguns.

items.name: ⬆️Ravana
items.description: Powercreep has caught up with this grandpa of a bot, but it’s still chugging along fairly well. A strict downgrade from UE Ravana, but still good in of itself. ⬆️If you have good reflexes, Ravana can be an incredibly difficult bot for Iaraghi builds to kill.

items.name: Raven
items.description: One of the best f2p attackers. Trades Imugi’s broken mobility and survivability tools for good mobility and notably higher damage potential.

items.name: ⬇️Skyros
items.description: An acceptable beacon runner that can be a pain in the ass to deal with, but powercreep has rendered it quite killable if focused down. ⬇️Skyros’ DMI and defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Loki
items.description: Similar to Skyros, but rather than being focused down, it needs to be QR’d. Can be incredibly annoying during the Titan phase if the team lacks QS titans.

items.name: ⬇️Leech
items.description: An inferior version of the ultimate, lacking DMI in ability but still having solid damage potential. ⬇️Leech’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Siren
items.description: Comparable to a Leech in terms of gameplay, but it trades mobility for target access. ⬇️Siren’s reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Scorpion
items.description: Inferior to the UE version, but still competent and may even be able to score assassination kills. That being said, unlike UE scorpion, your target can phase your stealth and attempt to outbrawl you, so you might have to just be satisfied with taking their deft survivor or force an ability use.

items.name: ⬆️Shenlou
items.description: Essentially a sidegrade of regular scorpion. ⬆️Shenlou can stack multiple shields behind each other, making it fairly difficult to kill with Iaraghi.

items.name: Samjok
items.description: Annoying beacon runner with a distinct class from Loki and Skyros, while it can’t stall beacons in phase, it can debuff enemies with the turret.

items.name: ⬆️Teth
items.description: While it has a disruptive EMP and decent sustain, the massive nerf to its BiW has rendered it rather immobile and thus hard to justify using over meta openers. ⬆️While Teth does rely on a forcefield, it also has regenerating physical shields in the front and back, providing it with decent protection against Iaraghi.

items.name: Ochokochi
items.description: A slight downgrade to Rex that trades a lot of raw stats for a pretty strong crowd control ability that can launch people off the map if timed right.

items.name: UE Mender
items.description: Can heal a bit of grey damage and stall a bit with DMI, built in revive, and high damage resistance.

items.name: Revenant
items.description: Similar to Ocho in that it can stall for a bit and recover to full health thanks to grey damage mitigation, but slightly worse.

items.name: ⬆️Ravager
items.description: A gunboat type robot that didn’t age too well since it doesn’t bring any damage boosts or utility (past the permanent stealth) to the table. ⬆️Ravager can stay in stealth and come out during Iaraghi downtime, making it both a good platform for Iaraghi and resilient to Iaraghi. Additionally, its short form factor makes it difficult to kill with blind fire, unlike Crisis.

items.name: Nightingale
items.description: A downgrade from Imugi, retaining the high uptime stealth and great speed in air, but trading the ability to shoot while flying for adjacent support capabilities, which honestly aren’t worth it.

items.name: Fafnir
items.description: Can theoretically become a menace if it gets charged up, but lacks any protection after the absorber drops, so it’s really hard to extract value out of.

items.name: SWORD Unit
items.description: You shouldn’t dash with the sword, it does NO damage and just puts you in danger. Treat it like a Siren and just teleport back to your translocator when the ability ends. The built in gun does respectable damage.

items.name: Ophion
items.description: Has high uptime on an absorber and a QR pilot, but doesn’t bring much else to the table.

items.name: Dagon
items.description: Similar to Ravager in that it’s a mediocre gunboat that doesn’t bring much to the table that bots in tiers above it can’t match or exceed.

items.name: Erebus
items.description: Unique 800m blackout ability that can disrupt people from behind cover across the map means it must be in this tier at minimum, but the rest of the bot leaves much to be desired.

items.name: ⬇️Harpy
items.description: The inferior 70% reflector (as compared to Siren’s 80%) has left this robot a full tier below since it can be easily shot down right through its protection. ⬇️Harpy’s reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Curie
items.description: Extra armorplates durability is meh, leaving it average durability in ability and extremely frail out of ability. Turret range is pretty short and damage is unimpressive by modern standards. Armorplates make it resistant to chip damage though, which is nice.

items.name: Orochi
items.description: The many buffs it has gotten have made Orochi technically usable, but it still suffers from major uptime issues after the first couple skirmishes.

items.name: UE Destrier
items.description: Technically has decent damage potential, but far below most UEs. The damage boost and weapon slots are unimpressive and the shield isn’t anything special, its only real benefit is the notably above average speed. The Kirk Sider pilot allows it to perform as a competent midranger when equipped with UE Ions. Unfortunately, Kirk leaves very little room for build customization, and you need every piece of the build in order for it to really function. Even then, Destrier is little more than a Dagon sidegrade.

items.name: UE Fujin
items.description: A relatively light frame with… brawler specialization? Wtf? It would be a tier higher if it had access to a nuclear amplifier, but as it stands it’s a fine robot with basically no modules.

items.name: UE Invader
items.description: An old powercrept ultimate that was never all too good. Not really recommended to invest in, as despite its price, its performance is around the level of f2p tanks. ⬇️UE Invader’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi and it is unlikely to get close enough to suppress the enemy.

items.name: Fury
items.description: Has no ability and low speed. The permanent shield breaker pilot is the only reason it's this high.

items.name: Behemoth
items.description: Essentially a Fury that trades the shieldbreaker pilot for an extra heavy and better stats. A direct (and major) downgrade from Bagliore.

items.name: Nether
items.description: Decently upgraded version of strider that is somewhat usable with the shieldbreaker pilot, but dies way too fast at close range.

items.name: ⬇️Fenrir
items.description: Outdated and slow tank, far inferior to the UE version. ⬇️Fenrir’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Typhon
items.description: Similar to Erebus but with a far inferior blackout and worse stats all around except for speed.

items.name: Khepri
items.description: While the healing is decent and the speed boost is unique, Khepri is a powercrept support and you'd be much better off using a Lio or Nuo instead.

items.name: ⬇️Phantom
items.description: Worse than Loki and Skyros at beacon running, worse than Scorpion and Shenlou at ambushing, worse than dedicated tanks at being a tank. Tries to do a little bit of everything, and it was a good jack of all trades back when it came out, but now it just ends up being pretty bad at everything. ⬇️Phantom’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬆️Condor
items.description: Shield charges enemy NA for free and healing isn't strong enough for it to properly survive in air. Weapon also got nerfed to shit so that can't even save it anymore. ⬆️Condor is surrounded by multiple regenerating shields, making it pretty strong against Iaraghi builds.

items.name: Angler
items.description: Angler has aged very poorly as a tank and it's far too slow to reasonably blind anyone unless you spawn right on them in beacon rush.

items.name: Ares
items.description: With the pilot it's fairly usable, but still loses to modern absorber bots and is extremely punishing to play due to how incredibly weak it is out of ability.

items.name: Blitz
items.description: Pretty outdated bot that relies on suppression to land in order to be able to fight. Decent when the enemy doesn't have some form of suppression immunity active.

items.name: ⬇️Falcon
items.description: Best described as “Skyros Pro Max” when running traditionalist. Regular Falcon is not really worth running. ⬇️Falcon’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Mender
items.description: Only in this tier for its mediocre grey healing, which isn't enough to keep up with modern health pools but still somewhat helpful.

items.name: ⬆️Weyland
items.description: Comparable tank to Fenrir that trades a bit of tankiness for additional supportive utility via healing. The pilot provides a very frail shield that can be rapidly activated and deactivated, useful for blocking high damage single shot attacks. ⬆️Weyland’s pilot shield can be used to absorb Iaraghi shots.

items.name: ⬇️Hellburner
items.description: Fast beacon capper that can’t do much else. Powercrept explosion, awful weapon slots, and low durability hold it back. The legendary pilot helps curb some of its weaknesses. ⬇️Hellburner’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Invader
items.description: One of the most unimpressive tanks in the game, having poor firepower and no real tanking ability aside from its suppression. ⬇️Invader’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi and it is unlikely to get close enough to suppress the enemy.

items.name: Nemesis
items.description: Really high shield uptime with a short cooldown, only held back by its poor firepower and lack of nuclear amplifier

items.name: Hades
items.description: The awkward middle child between Ares and Nemesis, being worse than both at pretty much everything.

items.name: Strider
items.description: Strict downgrade from Nether. Nether has a better version of Strider's damage on dash stacking pilot skill built in, in case you didn't know.

items.name: Inquisitor
items.description: Worse Raven.

items.name: Spectre
items.description: Worse Raven.

items.name: Pursuer
items.description: Outdated stats, outdated cooldown, and poor firepower make for a pretty mediocre bot.

items.name: Ao Jun
items.description: Outdated flying bot with an unreliable built in weapon and way too long of a cooldown on its ability.

items.name: Bulgasari
items.description: Bots relying on physical shields, dashes, or ancile shields are powercrept out of existence.

items.name: Haechi
items.description: Bots relying on physical shields, dashes, or ancile shields are powercrept out of existence.

items.name: Mercury
items.description: Significantly worse Raven.

items.name: Bulwark
items.description: Tanks relying on Aegis shields are not real.

items.name: Rayker
items.description: Can suppress... and do nothing much else.

items.name: ⬇️Ao Guang
items.description: Powercreep has gotten us to the point where it can be relatively easily killed in ability. It’s also pretty slow. ⬇️Ao Guang’s defense points are completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Tyr
items.description: A support that tries to flex into being an attacker. Was good back in the day, but now it's just a bad support and bad attacker.

items.name: Cerberus
items.description: Significantly downgraded Typhon.

items.name: ⬇️Seraph
items.description: Force field provides zero protection. Only good for extermination ⬇️Seraph’s forcefield is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Mars
items.description: Turret misses anything that is moving and not point blank range, plus outdated stats.

items.name: Jaeger
items.description: Worse than even Fury somehow.

items.name: ⬆️Shell
items.description: Free nuclear amplifier charger due to multiple shields being hit by splash damage. ⬆️Shell has multiple shields, allowing it to survive multiple Iaraghi shots, though it cannot regenerate them which puts it a bit behind newer shielded bots.

items.name: ⬇️Hawk
items.description: The beam does awful damage and has a long cooldown, tickling robots and titans alike. On top of that… Pixonic nerfed this already awful bot in the big 26 for no reason. It’s a Natasha Pro Max and the ability should be generally ignored. ⬇️Hawk’s reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Ao Qin
items.description: It has a good pilot that gives it stealth, but it lacks a proper specialization. Perhaps the best of the worst, but still unusable. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Kumiho
items.description: If only it could be bought with silver, this would be a decent early game beacon capper. Not worth spending gold on. Like Ao Qin and Hover, one of the less bad low tiers, but still unusable. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Hover
items.description: If only it could be bought with silver, this would be a decent early game beacon capper. Not worth spending gold on. Interestingly, it can fly eternally by spam pressing the ability quickly. Still a troll robot though. Like Ao Qin and Kumiho, one of the less bad low tiers, but still unusable. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Destrier
items.description: The first robot you obtain. You get what you (don’t) pay for. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Cossack
items.description: The second robot you obtain. Can run beacons until you get something better. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Schutze
items.description: A no longer obtainable meme robot with 1 heavy slot. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game. Personal favorite of Spiritings.

items.name: Gepard
items.description: A minor upgrade over Destrier that isn’t worth wasting gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: GI Patton
items.description: 4 pinatas allow for a cheap early game burst damage build. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Vityaz
items.description: A fairly versatile but ultimately outdated platform. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Golem
items.description: A no longer obtainable meme robot that was the first to feature one of each slot. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Boa
items.description: A no longer obtainable meme robot that was pretty bulky for its class (back in the day). All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Griffin
items.description: A decent silver workhorse with acceptable mobility and firepower until you find something better. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Rogatka
items.description: A usable beacon runner that isn’t worth spending silver on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Leo
items.description: The prime early game workhorse, costing silver and sporting both high firepower and durability (as far as super early game is concerned) with the default thunder/pinata setup being an okay brawler (again, in the super early game and nowhere else). All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Natasha
items.description: A Leo sidegrade, trading durability for additional firepower. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Rhino
items.description: An outdated heavy robot that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Stalker
items.description: An outdated light robot that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Carnage
items.description: An outdated glass cannon that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Fuijin
items.description: An outdated sentry that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Raijin
items.description: An outdated sentry that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Gareth
items.description: A minor upgrade over Destrier that isn’t worth wasting silver on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Galahad
items.description: For most early game purposes, Leo is preferred. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Lancelot
items.description: An outdated tank that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Jesse
items.description: Essentially a patton that trades the ability to hold all 4 mediums at once for extra speed. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Doc
items.description: While holding high firepower, it lacks the defenses to make much use out of it. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Butch
items.description: An okay early game midranger that can be bought with silver. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: Bolt
items.description: An outdated light robot that isn’t worth spending your gold on. All tier 2 and below (blue and grey) early game bots should be discarded ASAP as the lack of a specialization makes them unusable in the mid to late game.

items.name: ⬆️Sirocco
items.description: The single best brawler titan and the current meta flagship, it has not only an AoE Rust & EMP, but also a 14 second (!) Ravana-type phase shift that can be ended early. For 6 seconds after exiting phase, Sirocco gains absurd amounts of resistance and DMI, making it practically impossible to kill. And of course, the AoE Rust & EMP weapon deals way overtuned damage for what it is and can deal damage during phase. ⬆️Sirocco can close the distance between itself and an Iaraghi build with its long duration transcendence.

items.name: Bersagliere
items.description: Its incredible mobility and firepower allow it to be where it wants when it wants, making it similar to UE Ao Ming in that it can pick and choose fights on its own terms. Nearly permanent shieldbreaker uptime is a cherry on top that very few titans have access to. Tropical and Running Riot’s personal favorite.

items.name: ⬆️Princeps
items.description: Princeps has had plenty of time in the sun, and it’s fortunate to see that the nerfs don't completely kill it. Its nullfield uptime has been severely reduced, but godmode is godmode, so you better make those 6 seconds count. Also, its grav thrust hasn't been changed, so you can still fling people off the map! ⬆️Iaraghi builds cannot drain Princeps stasis barrier stacks early, meaning it has slightly longer protection against them.

items.name: UE Ao Ming
items.description: 4 Alphas enable powerful hybrid builds with long reload burst weapons on the back and sustained weapons on top. Otherwise, you can go all in with 4 sustained weapons or 4 burst weapons for a statchecking monster. Can pick and choose fights on its own terms as long as cover that it can fly over and land behind is present. Tanky and relatively resilient to fire from robots while on the ground, but vulnerable in air after the stealth from the legendary pilot expires. Both TRA and TNA are good choices. Adazahi’s personal favorite.

items.name: UE Murometz
items.description: Despite the fact that the UE Murometz simply has stronger stats and faster cooldowns than the regular Murometz, it is a considerably powerful damage platform that truly brings back the reign of terror our ancient titan had back in the day. Strong health, on-demand area of effect EMP, nearly perfected sustainability with the grey healing from the legendary pilot, and a playstyle that allows for easy use of UE TNA to make the titan exceptionally lethal each ability sweep. This titan can more or less be looked at as a sidegrade UE Ming, being better as a TNA damage dealer but worse as a TRA brawler.

items.name: ⬇️UE Minos
items.description: When played and built correctly, UE Minos is effectively a stronger and harder to counter version of Altas, with the same powerful EMP utility and very high mobility compared to other titans. Out of the highest ranking titans, UE Minos is the strongest beacon contester & staller by far. ⬇️UE Minos’ reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬆️Atlas
items.description: Absorbers on the sides and an occasional absorber in the front alongside good mobility and a powerful crowd control ability that can hold fast bots in place makes for an incredibly disruptive titan. Add on tanky stats and this is easily one of the best brawlers in the game. ⬆️Atlas’ permanent side shields can be used to protect itself from Iaraghi fire.

items.name: Bedwyr
items.description: Incredibly high uptime on a purple shield, tanky stats, and the most annoying taunt ability in the game make for an extremely solid brawler titan.

items.name: ⬆️Indra
items.description: Similar to Ravana, it has the powerful phase shift ability that allows it to dodge enemy uptime and fight on its own terms. That being said, it suffered a lot from its most recent nerf, so it’s no longer the single best f2p goat it used to be. ⬆️Similarly to Ravana, an Indra with good reflexes can be difficult to kill with Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Waymaker
items.description: Hunter stacks are still OP, and Waymaker’s Hunter stacks heal even more grey damage than Pathfinder’s, but the Titan pretty much doesn’t have anything else. The second ability is mid, and the opportunity cost of using this Titan just for Hunter stacks is too high considering you have 5 bots and 1 Titan. F2p’s should keep an eye on this titan as it very well may become the best f2p Titan in the game after it becomes readily accessible. ⬇️Waymaker’s counterblind triggers only after it dies to Iaraghi.

items.name: Mauler
items.description: One of the most broken abilities in the game (darklight) but it struggles to survive for long enough in situations where it’s needed. Still, good at shutting down brawlers through their defenses, though many top tier titans have ways of preventing darklight from ruining their game plan, so your darklight push will need to be very well planned and probably supported by a teammate in order to be successful.

items.name: Eiffel
items.description: The f2p version of UE Ao Ming. Instant burst weapons in the summoned slots add a ton of damage that can kill enemies before they have the chance to hit their deft survivor, and the mobility with the dash is comparable to even Bersagliere. The only downside is that it lacks protection and strongly relies on defensive motherships to make up for it.

items.name: UE Nodens
items.description: Similar to Waymaker, but it gives up the ability to stack teammates with damage boosting marks for more defensive personal stats and on-demand marginal grey healing/speed/defense boosts that don't require destroying a marked enemy.

items.name: 👥Newton
items.description: The lift ability can snag vulnerable enemies whose defensive ability is on cooldown from 800m away, exposing them to your team. 👥Newton itself is relatively defenseless, it really needs good teamplay to work. Plus one tier in squad play.

items.name: ⬇️Bjorn
items.description: Heavy duty brawler with high firepower but basically no mobility. An upgrade over Luchador in some aspects, mainly stalling potential due to titan last stand. ⬇️Bjorn’s DMI and resistance is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Luchador
items.description: Honestly worse than Minos at this point. All it has going for it is grey resistance and a bit more firepower. Otherwise, it’s slow, has long cooldowns, and subpar firepower. ⬇️Luchador’s reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Minos
items.description: Not significantly worse than UE Minos, honestly a really solid f2p brawler. Lacks the EMP and has a slightly weaker reflector as well as longer cooldowns, but stats wise, it actually has about the same effective HP as UE minos due to T3 damage resistance. ⬇️Minos’ reflector is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: ⬇️Aether
items.description: Has pretty strong protection in flight, though if you’re taking fire from multiple titans they may be able to brute force through it. Very weak on the ground and EMP takes forever to accumulate. ⬇️Aether’s forcefield is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Murometz
items.description: Trades off a lot of Aethers benefits (healing, speed, ability duration) for stealth in ability (which can sometimes be better and sometimes be worse) as well as an instant EMP, which is the main bread and butter of Muro. Played right, it can punch way above its weight class.

items.name: ⬆️Devourer
items.description: Mostly a support titan that can debuff enemies it links to. Needs the help of Bifrost or Stealther to have any impact itself, as its ability provides essentially no protection against titans. ⬆️Devourer is similar to Ravager in that it can wait until the Iaraghi has fired to come out of stealth. Unfortunately its essence shift defense is ignored by Iaraghi, and it can be blind fired due to its large hitbox.

items.name: ⬆️UE Arthur
items.description: Only in B tier because the shields protect against non-splash weaponry. Flames and Venires turn this thing into paste. It’s a regular edition Ming amount of health behind those shields, so you better pray you don’t run into anyone who is able to bypass them. ⬆️UE Arthur’s powerful physical shields can protect it from Iaraghi.

items.name: Nodens
items.description: Can remotely support other team mates with solid normal healing from a long range, but pretty niche since it does not heal gray damage. Suppression through walls is also occasionally helpful.

items.name: Heimdall
items.description: Mediocre brawler and usable support. The suppression rocket is not a reliable form of defense due to the prevalence of anticontrol/anti jamming turret.

items.name: ⬆️Rook
items.description: Due to the fairly mediocre but plentiful physical shields it possesses, rook serves to do little more than charge enemy nuclear amplifiers. That being said, it has fairly good mobility, comparable to that of Eiffel, so it can technically serve as an annoying beacon runner/staller lategame. ⬆️Rook has multiple regenerating physical shields as well as good mobility, allowing it to somewhat safely close the distance between itself and Iaraghi builds.

items.name: Sharanga
items.description: Outdated titan that went all in on firepower back in the day. Nowadays, titans can have the same amount of firepower it has (or more!) and also have actual impactful abilities.

items.name: Sirius
items.description: Awful support titan, huge hitbox, slow, neither ability actually does much of anything to support the team... don't invest in this thing, the only thing keeping it out of F tier is its modules.

items.name: Ao Ming
items.description: Used to be on par with Sharanga... before they took away its ability to have modules for no reason. Thanks Pixonic!

items.name: Arthur
items.description: Shares the nuclear amplifier charging issue with Rook, but lacks any of the mobility, specializations, or utility.

items.name: Kid
items.description: You get what you pay for and Kid is free. Don’t hurry to spend platinum on a mediocre titan to replace it though! The best way to escape Kid Hell is by saving up keys to spin titan chests in the black market.

items.name: Seeker
items.description: The ultimate generic drone, it’s so powerful that it competes with even some of the most OP tailor-made drones on their own robot - simply because being able to ignore stealth is that strong. You can use this drone on virtually any setup or robot in the game and it will be doing at least something for you, countereffects at a minimum.

items.name: Showdown
items.description: An extremely strong generic defensive drone that only needs level 4 to function. If your robot has stealth, that’s a bonus. Bots with grey damage resistance (ie Ammit and Lio) can abuse this drone hardcore.

items.name: ⬇️Armadillo
items.description: A f2p alternative to UE Glider, having a higher ceiling, but making you work much harder to get to the baseline amount of DP as UE Glider (and lacking the phase shift synergy) ⬇️Armadillo’s main ability is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Scourveil
items.description: Essentially an upgraded Kestrel, coming with a percentage damage shotgun instead of death marks, a far stronger grey heal on stealth, and a niche rust and EMP duration extension which is mostly just useful for Fang but not so restrictive as to be useless on other builds. It even extends the duration of effects from motherships like Mute!

items.name: UE Glider
items.description: Expensive as it is, UE Glider is a formidable generic defensive drone. Even in metas where UC is more powerful than phase shift, its non-phase related abilities are comparable to pre nerf Shai in terms of raw defense, so you can ignore the phase and just attach it to your bot for extra stats.

A.casual_name: Really strong but only on a few robots

items.name: ‼️Lar
items.description: The best option on regular edition Vulcan. Omen Vulcan should equip Webby instead. This drone is much more universal than some of the others released recently, as its last ability works on all bots and its other abilities individually work on a wide variety of bots, but only Vulcan can use both at once (and most bots that can use 2 of the abilities have better options). ‼️When equipped on 5+ slot robots with Boom/Bash/Pow, Lar’s deathmark can make them surprisingly deadly.

items.name: Kestrel
items.description: This drone is incredibly broken on certain bots (ie Imugi) due to how it can spam heals from its 4th ability. The death mark ability makes it generically good on close range bots, and it can even heal some grey damage on non-stealth bots as long as your mothership has Lifesaver equipped.

items.name: Myia
items.description: One of the most broken drones in the game, giving pretty much immunity to grey damage and an extremely OP built in weapon. Unfortunately, it only really works on a select few robots which go invisible.

items.name: Hawkeye
items.description: Gives reflector bots like UE Hawk and Vector shieldbreaker, as well as other appreciable features like extra mothership/titan charge and a slight bit of gray damage resistance. Very reliable in PVE.

items.name: Qingting
items.description: This drone is actually broken in certain circumstances, specifically on Pathfinder/Shoggoth for locking down Princeps towards the end of their ability before they get back to cover. However, it's pretty useless for anything but this niche. Qingting currently has a bug that makes it OP. It is not ranked for that purpose and should not be used that way.

items.name: Bull
items.description: A very strong built in weapon paired with the only additional source of DoT resistance in the game makes this drone an easy pick on DoT converters like Rex, Ocho, and UE Rhino.

items.name: Aopo
items.description: Literally only in this tier for its use on Nuo. No other bot wants this drone, but it's best in slot on Nuo. Not even Lio, who prefers Showdown.

items.name: Freezo
items.description: Extremely broken defensive drone, able to stack 300+ defense points and 90% grey damage resistance. Unfortunately, it only fully works on Pathfinder and partially works on Shoggoth + UE Rayker.

items.name: Webby
items.description: The strongest debuffing drone in the game, as its weapon can apply 100% rust effect. Unfortunately it only activates when used on Dux, Imugi, and Omen Vulcan (and Fafnir I guess).

items.name: Solar
items.description: Allows you to melt people from across the map with snipers thanks to its defense penetration, but is seriously restricted to only a small subset of weapons and only activates if there is an enemy further than 700m available to shoot. Also has a pretty long cooldown.

items.name: Fhtagn
items.description: Enhances hunter stacks and grants partial defense breach + full defense mitigation against marked targets 600m away. It's like a better version of the Solar drone, but only for Pathfinder and Shoggoth (and Pathfinder still really wants Freezo)

items.name: ⬇️Scales
items.description: Only really ideal on Ammit, though it's technically a universal drone, most bots that don’t have a specific drone would much rather use just about any other universal drone. ⬇️Scales’ main ability is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Hiruko
items.description: While this drone is an acceptable universal drone and a decent specific drone for Rex and Ochokochi, the main reason it is this high is due to its value when used on UE Rhino. UE Rhino doesn’t really need bull since it is already damn near unkillable in ability, so Hiruko’s damage boosting ability helps offset its poor firepower.

items.name: Kocho
items.description: The generally ideal pick for Kaji, though Myia is probably comparable to it even on Kaji (whereas Kocho is unfortunately not particularly useful for Anaksor).

items.name: Prena
items.description: Provides Dedopali with even more damage output and a bit of movement utility, which is actually pretty valuable for the robot as it doesn’t have access to a nuclear amplifier and is rather slow. Myia is strong competition against it, but overall Prena is likely to be the best in-slot for Dedopali. Prena also boosts all BIWs by 25% additional damage, even if the BIW isn’t a “remote” weapon (take Hastatus, Condor, Anaksor, Sword, and others for example), so the drone does actually have a decent amount of use cases on things that don’t have invisible/apply gravity lift.

items.name: Object
items.description: A good drone option for Nekton while still being kind of technically usable on other flying/jumping robots, namely flying robots that also have absorber shielding. Unfortunately, the powerful grey healing ability can be inconsistent and awkward to trigger, as it requires Nekton to cancel its flight very early on AND also have taken a lot of damage to its absorber during a short flight.

items.name: Shai
items.description: Had a far fall from grace after getting nerfed pretty badly. Still usable if you have a maxed one from back in the day, but not worth investing in.

items.name: ⬆️Reviver
items.description: Cheap drone that can save your ass even without much investment. Unfortunately it doesn’t do anything for you before or after its single activation. ⬆️Provides two sources of one time protection from Iaraghi

items.name: Whiteout
items.description: Very powerful and generic f2p drone, providing any close range damage dealer with an EMP that can disrupt nearby enemies and a heal that can come in handy. Can be competitive with Seeker (but still typically worse) on bots with a teleport such as Scorpion or Demeter, since it lets you properly time an EMP trigger at the right moment.

items.name: Glider
items.description: An okay defensive drone for robots running phase shift. Similarly to other drones in this tier, while its abilities are pretty nice, the opportunity cost is a bit too high to justify using it.

C.casual_name: Good for a few bots, bad otherwise

items.name: Ward
items.description: BiW misses anything that is moving and not in close range. Lockdown ability takes a while. 4th ability damage boost is bugged and doesn’t do anything (since it was last tested). That being said, it can be used just for the strong weapon if you're running a build that fights at a close enough range that it actually hits (or a build that can lock people down) but the opportunity cost is too high for it to ever be optimal. Also, it's an unobtainable collab item.

items.name: Moderator
items.description: Has a niche on bots like UE Ao Jun (allows instant lock upon reaching max flight altitude) and Crisis, but is easily replaceable on both.

items.name: Daltokki
items.description: Decent generic drone that gives some helpful damage and speed boosts when using modules. The main issue with this drone is that it doesn’t do much on robots that use Phase Shift, and most robots want to use Phase Shift.

items.name: Tensor
items.description: Nerfed in addition to the fact that it’s arguably not even worthwhile to use anymore on the robots that do have reflectors, as they could use Hawkeye instead or just a different universal drone in the first place.

items.name: ⬇️Ironhearth
items.description: Has a niche on Khepri, Revenant, and UE Revenant, since these bots can give themselves freeze immunity and trigger the drone’s defense ability. Never use this as a generic drone, only bots that can grant themselves immunity to blast and/or freeze can make use of it. Additionally, Immune amplifier completely breaks this drone and causes it to stop triggering after reaching 20 stacks, so to function on Revenant/UE Revenant, they must equip last stand, which is probably not worth doing on UE Revenant. ⬇️Ironhearth’s main ability is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Paralysis
items.description: Niche drone that can lock people down when used with certain weapons with high fire rates (ie Bendy Bullets)

items.name: Barrel
items.description: Barrel can give the equivalent of a free pathfinder stack every time you go below 30% HP. Unfortunately, it rarely triggers more than a couple times per match, not because of the difficulty in surviving while at 30% HP and making a full recovery (it's actually quite trivial on bots with strong grey healing) but because of its 40 second cooldown between activations. The actual explosion part of Barrel should be considered a bonus and you never play around it.

items.name: ⬇️Beak
items.description: Instant stealth when taking a small amount of damage is nice, but the duration is far too short and cooldown is far too long to be competitive. ⬇️Beak’s stealth won’t get to trigger before you die to an Iaraghi shot.

items.name: Chongue
items.description: Poor drone with mostly unimpactful abilities. The somewhat noticeable speed boost on Phase is the only justification for using it, as it can make Ravana very fast, but the opportunity cost is way too high.

items.name: ⬇️Nebula
items.description: Strict activation condition and long cooldown on an outdated ability. ⬇️Nebula’s shield won’t get to trigger before you die to an Iaraghi shot.

items.name: Pascal
items.description: A relatively mediocre survivalist drone. Its damage ability only works on Curie (and doesn’t do much for it at that) and its protective abilities are outclassed by many other defensive drones.

items.name: Wave
items.description: Built-in weapon with grey damage that rarely hits, paper thin shields every time you lose a physical shield, and a slight boost to flight speed are not enough to justify taking your drone slot.

items.name: Patron
items.description: Blind is not common enough to justify using a drone that literally does nothing if you don't get blinded.

items.name: Scarabeus
items.description: The only real ability this drone has is the 50% increase to physical shield durability, which really isn’t worth your drone slot.

items.name: The Eye
items.description: Death mark with a long cooldown, not worth leveling up to the point where it unlocks that ability anyways.

items.name: Starter
items.description: Minor healing ability, the go to option if you have nothing else.

items.name: Persephone
items.description: Mechanic pilot skill type healing, not worth using as your drone, just use mechanic.

items.name: Defender
items.description: Weak ancile, powercrept.

items.name: Good Guy
items.description: Weak aegis, powercrept.

items.name: Discus
items.description: Conditional minor speed boosts that aren’t worth using a drone slot for.

items.name: Octanian
items.description: Weak built in weapon that can't actually lock anything down without hitting every single bullet. Also, it’s an unobtainable collab item.

items.name: Wasp
items.description: Weak built in weapon and nothing else.

items.name: Sharpshooter
items.description: Wasp but with an even worse weapon.

items.name: Fly
items.description: Active ability that is worse than most drone passive abilities.

items.name: Roswell
items.description: A peculiar mothership that lifts your robot up, gives you 80% DoT resistance, converts all damage you take into DoT, and gives a 25% damage boost as a cherry on top. Almost like Pixonic knew that DoT conversion would be useful in a meta dominated by Iaraghi, as it's one of the only ways to resist their damage. The turret slots are also great, 2 protection and 1 support. This is basically the Bifrost replacement.

items.name: ⬇️Bifrost
items.description: Provides 10 seconds of damage resistance and DMI which allow you to be safe from enemies with standard penetration (ie titan weapons) or antistealth. To top it off, it also gives one free cleanse stack. Better suited for titans, but still good on regular robots as a means of defense. Also has great turret slots, 2 protection 1 support. ⬇️Bifrost protection is completely ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: 👥Mute
items.description: Solid mothership that functions as a hybrid between an offense and a defense mothership, as it both provides protection via blind and makes the enemy vulnerable via EMP. Countered by the anti-jamming turret and/or cleanse stacks, though. 👥Really powerful in sweaty squad games as it can completely shut down a group of bots for a long time, but hard to get as much value out of it without coordination. Plus one tier in squad play.

items.name: Avalon
items.description: Provides decent grey healing and 3 cleanse stacks. Braindead ship that you can comfortably use as soon as you have it charged. Good turret slots (2 protection 1 support) which allow for several good builds.

items.name: Frederick
items.description: Gives massive damage and speed boosts for a short duration that allow you to catch people by surprise and kill them incredibly quickly. 1 attack and 2 support turret slots aren’t bad, but the lack of a protection slot makes you very vulnerable to being shut down by the enemy responding by simply activating a defensive mothership or blinding/suppressing you.

items.name: Paladin
items.description: A fairly unique defensive ship that provides a strong Aegis which grants some grey healing if it isn’t destroyed after 8 seconds. Unfortunately, in this day and age, the aegis is likely to break unless you go out of your way to hide while it’s active.

items.name: Stealther
items.description: Stealther now only has 1 second of stealth advantage over the lifesaver turret. The green healing is still decent, but most defensive motherships offer more than just +1 second of stealth, and honestly, all that keeps this ship this high now is the double support turrets (and one protection turret) that it has.

items.name: Thor
items.description: An attack ship that not only does a very large amount of damage, but also completely disables enemy shields if they’re touched by it. Since escaping it doesn’t give them their shield back, it’s a fairly reliable effect and the only way to give titans shieldbreaker if they don’t have it built into their kit or pilot. Unfortunately, it has 2 attack slots, but it does have a protection slot, which lets you at least equip lifesaver.

items.name: R’lyeh
items.description: A modern version of Roulette that permanently reduces the maximum durability of enemies caught in its vortex. This is notably the only ship worth using Gravity Amplifier on as an interaction between them causes it to reduce maximum durability even more, so the two attack slots aren’t that big of a downside. The issue is the same as roulette; most enemies can escape the vortex fairly easily.

items.name: Roulette
items.description: Conditionally helpful ship attack ship that reduces enemy healing, which can help take down tanks, but a whole mothership slot for this isn’t justified, and it's easy to escape the rust field. Has really strong turret slots, though, two support and one protection, which is rare among attack ships.

items.name: Keel
items.description: One of the better attack ships in the game. Still doesn’t deal grey damage, but is useful for finishing off low health targets that got to cover or harassing low HP bots since phase shift can only save you from one of the three strikes. Still very difficult to justify taking over a defense ship.

items.name: Northlight
items.description: Old powercrept defense ship. Provides a burst of healing that overflows into an aegis when you’re fully healed, as well as some defense points. Its effect is much weaker than the effects of modern defense ships. Kept afloat by the fact that it has both a protection and support turret slot. Also has an attack slot, which is rare among defensive ships.

items.name: Mantis
items.description: Powercrept defense ship. Provides minor healing and an aegis. Kept afloat by the fact that it has both a protection and support turret slot.

items.name: Frozen Scorn
items.description: Awful attack ship, deals bad damage, is easy to escape, and the effect it applies is unimpressive. The only thing keeping this ship afloat is that it has 1 support and 2 protection slots, which is quite good, but the actual main effect of the ship sucks, and many ships have these slots PLUS an actually good effect.

items.name: Beholder
items.description: Bad attack ship that does no grey damage. Only really useful for finishing off low health targets that got to cover or harassing lighter backline bots. The beam tracks enemies around, but the damage is pitiful if they run away from it. Additionally this ship has double attack slots, which is not a good thing.

items.name: Sekhem
items.description: Really bad attack ship. The concept is that it bombards a large area, but 90% of the time, only the main payload hits, and that by itself is weaker than other attack ships. Additionally this ship has double attack slots, which is not a good thing.

items.name: Orion
items.description: Incredibly outdated attack ship that does no gray damage and has double attack slots, which is not a good thing.

items.name: Monarch
items.description: Extremely bad attack ship that does no grey damage and only has two turret slots, one of which is attack.

items.name: Dreadnought A42
items.description: You get what you (didn’t) pay for. This ship doesn’t do anything, replace it with anything else as soon as you can.

items.name: Lifesaver
items.description: While some may argue that Durability Extender belongs in this tier, the fact is that Durability Extender has competition and Lifesaver does not. There are literally only two reasons to ever not use lifesaver; either you're using Stealther, or you have a lifesaver equipped already without benefiting from drones that activate perks based on Stealth (Kestrel, Scourveil, Showdown, etc). This turret does not stack stealth duration if you use multiple.

items.name: Durability Extender
items.description: This turret can make you nearly unkillable in the endgame after you've used your mothership enough times, as it constantly stacks you with additional durability. Becomes broken when double stacked on motherships with two support slots.

A.casual_name: Prevent scalers from scaling to thanos

items.name: Damage Enforce System
items.description: Turret that provides a huge 50% damage boost for 10 seconds. Its only downside is that it has to compete with durability extender.

items.name: Positive Energy Recuperator
items.description: This turret is not high thanks to its okayish speed boost, but rather thanks to its lockdown and slowdown immunities. Lockdown and slowdown immunity are nice to have in a pinch.

B.casual_name: Use w/ Lifesaver if 2 protection slots

items.name: Anti-Jamming Support
items.description: This turret is the best one to use in protection slots that aren't occupied by Lifesaver. It provides you with 15 seconds of immunity to blind, suppression, and EMP, which can be lifesaving.

items.name: Lockdown Blast Cannon
items.description: This turret is the best one to use in attack slots due to the utility of lockdown. Fun fact, it can lock down targets through stasis barrier, just like Pathfinder & Shoggoth.

items.name: ⬆️Enhanced Aegis System
items.description: Provides a decent 150,000 HP slim shield, though in high level play it breaks pretty quickly. ⬆️Can tank a shot of Iaraghi for you.

items.name: ⬆️Aegis Blast System
items.description: Similar to enhanced aegis system, but the shield has a measly 36,000 HP and is a bubble rather than a slim shield, making it easier for enemies to shoot it off you. Also gives the shield to nearby teammates, which is cool. ⬆️Can tank a shot of Iaraghi for you.

items.name: ⬆️Aegis Self System
items.description: A weaker version of Aegis Blast System with a measly 12,000 HP and it doesn’t share the shield with teammates. ⬆️Can tank a shot of Iaraghi for you.

items.name: ⬇️Defender System
items.description: Provides 100 defense points for 10 seconds. May be viable on Bifrost builds that are anticipating that every enemy you face will have quantum radar, but generally still not worth using over Lifesaver. ⬇️Defense points are Ignored by Iaraghi.

items.name: Sonic Bomb Cannon
items.description: Decent attack turret thanks to grey damage, but not worth taking over the lockdown utility of lockdown blast cannon. Only use it on double attack slots where you already have a lockdown cannon equipped.

items.name: Gravity Amplifier
items.description: The slowdown is literally unnoticeable, this turret barely does anything for its intended use. It has exactly one use case on R’lyeh specifically due to an interaction between turrets and mothership effects which allows it to increase the percentage durability reduction done by that mothership. Outside of that one use case you should never pick it.

items.name: Periodic Fix Station
items.description: Minor healing, not good.

items.name: Repair Blast Station
items.description: Arguably worse than default support turret because it repairs flat HP rather than percentage HP, though it does also heal people near you.

items.name: Laser Blast Cannon
items.description: Pew pew gun that does bad damage in an area, no grey damage.

items.name: Target Ray Cannon
items.description: Downgraded Laser Blast Cannon that only deals damage to one player, and deals less damage.

items.name: 👁️Iaraghi L, 👁️Iaraghi M, 👁️Iaraghi H
items.description: I’m not sure what we as the playerbase did to deserve weapons this broken being added to the game, but here we are I guess. Only the most sturdy of brawlers and titans with high base HP can tank a couple shots, as they ignore all resistance-based defense systems including reflectors, DMI, and last stand. You can only hope to not get targeted, hide with stealth, dodge them, or block them with a shield. 👁️These weapons are so absurdly overpowered that the meta is being bent around their existence. The vast majority of [⬆️] and [⬇️] tags are based on the performance of bots/titans against these weapons.

items.name: Mesmer L, Mesmer M, Mesmer H
items.description: Strong weapons that combine into a single AoE beam that fires out of the center of your robot’s hitbox. This allows you to reliably blindfire virtually ANY stealthed or invisible enemy that’s at the same elevation as your robot, though it comes at the cost of the ability to corner shoot. They also steadily accumulate blastcharge, which makes the weapons decent at chipping the health of super durable/high defense point targets.

items.name: Lumen L, Lumen M, Lumen H
items.description: Laser type weapons that deal lower damage than the others in X tier, but make up for it by bending around corners to hit anyone within 600m and combine a large mag with a fast reload to have very little downtime.

items.name: Velos, Machaira, Basileus
items.description: Among the best 500m weapons in the game, dealing solid damage at midrange and also being the best support weapons in the game thanks to their powerful rust and fragility debuffs.

items.name: Harmattan L, Harmattan M, Harmattan H
items.description: Percentage damage shotguns. Imagine a cross between ARMs and Hammer/Mace/Cudgel. A single one added as supplementary damage to another close range build can pack an incredible punch against high HP high resistance targets.

items.name: UE Storm, UE Gust
items.description: Easy mag handling with reload while firing mechanics, absurdly strong burst damage, and decent accuracy to top it off makes these shotguns meta defining.

items.name: UE Arm L, UE Arm M
items.description: Similar to UE Machineguns in that they can ignore heavily armored targets, but take it a step further in being able to ignore even DMI. Unfortunately, their damage seriously tapers off as the enemy gets lower on HP, so they struggle to finish enemies off. Still, they are incredible at force proc’ing TRA and getting beefy enemies low enough for a teammate to clean up.

items.name: UE Incinerator, UE Scald
items.description: Solid damage at 500m with good splash and projectile speed. Blast is a nice added benefit against heavily armored targets.

items.name: UE Shredder
items.description: A light weapon that deals DPS comparable to many heavy weapons and locks down as well. Its only real limit is the terrible accuracy, but it’s great when used at close range.

items.name: UE Taran
items.description: A random silent buff doubled their damage, reverting them to their prime pre-nerf state and catapulting them back into X tier. UE Tarans are outstanding close range weapons, and while they lose out to shotguns, their perfect accuracy and fast projectiles at 350m range makes them both dangerous and reliable.

items.name: Murix, Elox
items.description: Deadly shotguns at point blank, but tickle at further distances.

items.name: Piercer
items.description: Currently the best sniper in the game, but unfortunately restricted to the heavy slot.

items.name: ‼️Liodari, ‼️Kroko, ‼️Hippo
items.description: Possess extremely high burst damage, but not so much so that they own the entire meta quite like they did before they were nerfed. ‼️These weapons charge titans incredibly quickly, making them often worth using over higher tier weapons despite the damage difference simply because they enable you to drop your titan early.

items.name: UE Toxin, UE Venom
items.description: These weapons deal insane amounts of DoT damage, which ignores all defense systems. However, due to their awful direct damage and the nature of DoT dealing fully repairable damage, they pretty much require high uptime shieldbreaker and/or Webby’s rust effect in order to function properly, which limits their build options.

items.name: UE Punisher T
items.description: Niche weapon that can tear through enemies that rely on defense points and lack DMI. Can be exceptionally strong against TNA titans, and can even hurt TRA titans after their DMI has expired. Pairs well with percentage damage weapons.

items.name: UE Wasp
items.description: Good sustained damage 600m weapon thanks to its large mag.

items.name: UE Pulsar
items.description: Essentially a UE Wasp that trades magsize for lockdown and slightly better burst damage.

items.name: UE Ion
items.description: Really solid burst damage at 600m, but suffers if enemies get close due to it's downtime while reloading.

items.name: UE Redeemer
items.description: Solid burst and sustained damage 350m weapons with fast mothership charge and fast projectile speed.

items.name: UE Corona, UE Glory, UE Halo
items.description: Downgraded UE Storms. Do less damage and have worse range, but can apply lockdown.

items.name: UE Cryo, UE Glacier, UE Rime
items.description: Burst rocket launchers that can apply freeze. They share many of the same downsides as their regular counterparts (unreliable slow projectiles and a longer reload) but they are nonetheless dangerous at close range. UE Cryo is notable as the best weapon in the game that can fully trigger the defense effect of the Freezo drone on Pathfinder.

items.name: UE Tempest
items.description: Autocannon with questionable performance at long range due to the slow projectiles. Nonetheless, at close to mid range, this weapon outputs very competitive damage. Outperforms its medium counterpart by more than it should.

items.name: ArmM, ArmL
items.description: Downgrades to their UE variants that still hold up pretty well.

items.name: Deshret, Hedjet, Pshent
items.description: Weird weapons that can do a lot of burst and even hurt people through walls. Unfortunately, they trade a decent bit of damage for this utility.

items.name: Pulsar
items.description: Respectable damage with the ability to lockdown. Officially now an upgrade to Hazard due to the rebalance. If only we could say the same about Magnetar…

items.name: UE Molot T
items.description: Poorly scaled damage compared to UE Tempest, but does basically the same thing otherwise. Decent at midrange, questionable at the advertised 800m. Unfortunately outclassed by a lot of other midrange medium options, so it should only really be used alongside UE Tempest and not by itself.

items.name: UE Orkan
items.description: A solid burst rocket launcher with acceptable splash.

items.name: UE Blaze, UE Igniter
items.description: Subpar damage for ultimate weapons that are very much prone to missing due to slow projectiles. The slow effect they apply helps curb this slightly.

items.name: UE Calamity, UE Scourge
items.description: Solid at close range, tickle at range. These are "jack of all trades" weapons that feel alright to use, but are somewhat unimpressive by today's standards. The only reason they are even one tier above their regular counterparts is due to the fact that they don’t have that annoying outdated lock-on mechanic.

items.name: UE Shocktrain
items.description: Similar to UE Ion, but they trade off 100m range and a bit of damage for instant unload.

items.name: UE Vortex
items.description: Ridiculous damage that's almost impossible to actually see in game due to how horrid their accuracy is. Essentially require lockdown (ie Pathfinder) to perform. Can be used on builds that get up to point blank and fire them, but I wouldn’t really recommend doing this because one sidestep or phase shift is all it takes to make you do zero damage.

items.name: UE Tulumbas
items.description: Their DPS is pretty awful, but their splash is still huge, allowing them to cheese people around corners and force them out of cover.

items.name: UE Havoc, UE Scatter, UE Devastator
items.description: The UE version of these weapons only beat the regular version by virtue of magazine size and reload. The burst DPS is pretty much the same.

items.name: UE Avenger
items.description: The nerf has left these weaker than their medium counterpart. They are still usable, but easily replaceable by better weapons (ie percentage damage weapons), even for anti-titan builds.

items.name: UE Atomizer
items.description: An incredibly awkward Atomizer-Arbiter hybrid that is difficult to extract value out of. If used at medium range, it’s actually worse than regular Atomizer due to the very short burst duration and unimpressive DPS. However, if you fully overheat it and used it as a point-blank face brawling weapon, it deals competent sustained damage. Unfortunately, the accuracy is so horrible while overheating it that you basically need to be touching the enemy to actually do damage, and the burst damage is unimpressive compared to other weapons at that range.

items.name: Kelvin, Fahrenheit, Celsius
items.description: Close range flamethrowers with okay damage, good splash, and the ability to curve around walls. Basically just the modern day T3 flamethrowers.

items.name: Howler, Growler, Screamer
items.description: Trade the burst of sonic shotguns for better sustain and more range. Really nice on many builds, and typically my go-to recommendation for f2p.

items.name: Voonith, Urhag, Shantak
items.description: One of the weirdest nerfed weapons in the game, as their overall effectiveness and handling was crippled but the individual amount of damage they deal per shot at range was increased. It’s one of those cases where it’s annoying to use but also annoying to fight against, since they are still technically a threat, just an easily ignorable one. Generally, these weapons are worse than the Hwangje/Yeoje/Taeja family in terms of damage, but their massive projectiles allow them to hit stealthed or cloaked enemies.

items.name: Nucleon, Atomizer, Quarker
items.description: A F2p staple. These weapons output consistent damage and are flexible, working from 500m to point blank. They trade some DPS and the full grey damage of Howler family for better performance at range.

items.name: Cudgel, Hammer, Mace
items.description: Decent f2p weapons with surprisingly good damage at a moderate distance, but they're best used at close range.

items.name: Devastator, Havoc, Scatter
items.description: Inferior versions of the ultimate editions, able to do high burst grey damage but lack sustain. Mostly better than cudgel/hammer/mace, except for at range.

items.name: Kirin, Mogwan, Gangil
items.description: Decent shotguns with a supportive rust + crumble effect and strong burst damage, but mediocre sustain.

items.name: Blight, Decay, Hazard
items.description: The go-to f2p 600m range weapons.

items.name: Subduer, Tamer, Damper
items.description: : Trades some of Decay's range for the rust effect. Decent damage for a f2p weapon.

items.name: ‼️Hwangje, ‼️Taeja, ‼️Yeoje
