items.description: Acceptable damage and long range. ‼️Drones like Solar or Fhtagn are recommended to make these weapons more lethal at range. Harold Han is especially important as he matches their unload time to Solar’s damage and penetration effect duration.

items.name: Pilum, Gladus
items.description: 600m range niche weapons nerfed to f2p level performance (comparable to Decay family).

items.name: Splinter, Shatter, Brisant
items.description: These weapons are something like Cudgel/Hammer/Mace but more specialized to be used at range. Which is weird, because they are shotguns. Not really bad, but their only use case is specifically around 200m range, where they are the best shotguns. At further or closer ranges, they are outperformed.

items.name: Glacier, Cryo, Rime
items.description: Very competitive burst damage but with several downsides. Not only do their slow projectile speed make them unreliable at longer ranges or against quickly moving targets, but they also have a very long reload and unforgivingly short burst. On top of that, they have ultimate weapon scaling, so you’ll need to take them to mk2 level 12 in order for them to perform at this level.

items.name: Shredder
items.description: In a higher tier than Puncher thanks to its much better effectiveness at range. Solid light weapon option with consistent lockdown at a medium distance.

items.name: Calamity, Scourge, Spark
items.description: Old weapons that have been given enough buffs to become somewhat serviceable. Their main downside is the lock-on mechanic, which requires you to take the guidance operator pilot skill in order for them to not feel awful to use (and even then, you’re still stuck with a somewhat annoying 1 second lock on time).

items.name: ‼️Bash, ‼️Boom, ‼️Pow
items.description: Can be annoying in TDM, but they are incredibly clunky for most builds. ‼️Very dangerous when used with 5+ slot robots and Lar, especially on Vulcan, as the BiW can apply the death mark and cause them to oneshot most enemies.

items.name: Morana, Chione, Jotunn
items.description: 600m weapons that are okay on paper, but aside from straight up worse damage than Decay family, they also are prone to missing a lot, and their arcing trajectory is only useful on a couple maps (ie Moon).

items.name: Gauss, Volt, Weber
items.description: While ignoring defense points is a gimmick with a ton of potential, railguns are rarely worth using due to how unimpressive their damage is.

items.name: Puncher
items.description: Decent damage at point blank with built in lockdown, but awful accuracy and a bit worse damage than the point blank weapons in the tier above it.

items.name: ‼️Porthos, ‼️Athos, ‼️Aramis
items.description: Perfect accuracy and decent burst damage at 350m, but their sustained damage leaves much to be desired, making them suboptimal for brawlers who would much appreciate the healing they provide. ‼️Since they can help repair your bot’s chip damage, they have use cases on burst damage dealers that appreciate repairs such as Leech and Siren.

items.name: Claw, Jaw, Talon
items.description: Support weapons with a strong effect (fragility can reduce defense points through DMI!), usable damage, and an arcing trajectory similar to the Morana family. Unfortunately, they are prone to missing, especially when there is an elevation difference (ie you are in a flying bot). Their buff gave them new life... but they need a little more to truly be worth it.

items.name: Incinerator, Scorcher, Scald
items.description: At very low investment, these weapons are decent since they mostly do damage through the blast effect, which ignores all forms of protection and doesn’t scale with level (though the effect accumulation does).

items.name: Redeemer
items.description: Used to be a top tier f2p 350m weapon, but ever since its nerf, it has become hard to justify using as it is outclassed by even some 500m weapons. The main benefit is that the fast projectiles it fires makes it feel very reliable and consistent to use.

items.name: Nanea, Leinani
items.description: Pretty much just worse versions of weapons from the Decay family.

items.name: Hornet, Wasp
items.description: Solid burst damage at 600m, but awfully long reload. Just use the Decay family instead.

items.name: Kramola, Razdor, Smuta
items.description: Homing machineguns that go around corners but have an awfully long reload and subpar damage. Not terrible, and have niche circumstances where they can force enemies out of cover, but still not really worth using.

items.name: Cestus, Ksiphos, Labrys
items.description: 500m weapons with meh damage and occasional blasts.

items.name: Avenger, Punisher T, Punisher
items.description: Outdated machine guns, but they're cheap as hell, do okay damage, and often your last resort. Poor accuracy as you approach their maximum range.

items.name: Corona, Halo, Glory
items.description: While these shotguns have damage comparable to that of some of the good f2p shotguns, their range is atrocious, dealing as little as half their damage or less the moment you step out of point blank range.

items.name: Exodus
items.description: Outdated rocket launcher with surprisingly good burst but an absurdly long reload.

items.name: ⬆️GAS
items.description: In the vast majority of circumstances, it is not worth trading a medium weapon for a shield. Nonetheless, there are a few bots that appreciate this “weapon” (ie. Fang). ⬆️GAS can absorb an Iaraghi shot for you every so often, which is nice.

items.name: Trebuchet
items.description: Long range with some of the highest damage per bullet in the game. Unfortunately, it has an insanely long reload. These weapons may prove to be semi-usable in certain metas that favor damage dealt in a single shot.

items.name: Tempest
items.description: Usable damage but its claim of 800m range is quite deceptive; the accuracy gets pretty bad past 350m. A sidegrade of Avenger that trades damage for better accuracy (because even though its accuracy sucks, it's still better than Avenger's).

items.name: Viper
items.description: Outdated energy machine gun. A bit weaker than Avenger but with better accuracy and some damage as DoT.

items.name: Regulator
items.description: 800m weapon with pretty awful damage.

items.name: Blaze, Ember, Igniter
items.description: Outdated and overnerfed flamethrowers with poor accuracy due to slow projectiles.

items.name: Shocktrain
items.description: Outdated zap gun, clunky lock on with damage that isn't really worth it.

items.name: Hel, Skadi, Snaer
items.description: Outdated and overnerfed 600m weapons that used to be f2p staples

items.name: Dragoon, Hussar, Marquess
items.description: Outdated and overnerfed 600m weapons that used to be f2p staples

items.name: Magnetar
items.description: Tiny magsize. For some reason, when seeing that this weapon was performing the same as its medium counterpart Pulsar, rather than buffing Pulsar, they crippled magnetar.

items.name: Sting
items.description: Surprisingly, this weapon performs comparably to Marquess.

items.name: ⬆️Needle, ⬆️Spike, ⬆️Stake
items.description: Their best use case is unironically just their paper thin shield that can block a single big shot, their damage is awful, never use these weapons for their damage. One could potentially justify using Needle on a light slot if they had no other choice, but the heavier counterparts can only really be justified on weapons that are constantly stowed (ie Spike on Fafnir top slots). ⬆️Needle, Spike, and Stake provide an energy shield that can absorb an Iaraghi shot.

items.name: ‼️Shifang, ‼️Fengbao, ‼️Leiming
items.description: These weapons have the benefits of locking down, ignoring stealth, and hitting multiple enemies at once, but their damage and range is awful. ‼️These weapons charge titans incredibly quickly, making them often worth using over higher tier weapons despite the damage difference simply because they enable you to drop your titan early.

items.name: Flux
items.description: The damage is incredibly bad (comparable to weapons in F tier) though it has notably exceptional mothership charge accumulation which is why it’s in D tier.

items.name: Smite, Discipline
items.description: Good luck hitting anything with these. Aside from having poor damage, they can’t actually hit their target most of the time.

items.name: Storm, Gust
items.description: Outdated shotguns that aged slightly better than Thunder. Technically usable burst DPS but with awful range, no utility, and an incredibly long reload.

items.name: UE Dragoon, UE Hussar
items.description: Ultimates that were unjustly nerfed to hell twice over. Not worth investing in for anyone, as they yield awful results despite their price.

items.name: Bane, Toxin, Venom
items.description: DoT weapons are only good if their DoT is incredibly strong. As you might be able to guess...these weapons have fairly weak DoT.

items.name: Avalanche
items.description: Outdated and overnerfed 500m rocket launcher. Notably large splash range but its mag is so small and its damage is so bad that it doesn’t matter.

items.name: Spear
items.description: Similar damage to Magnum but with more range. Not really a big enough difference to justify a full tier increase over Magnum though.

items.name: Reaper
items.description: Way overnerfed sniper with awful damage and a long reload. Doesn't even matter that it does true damage. Also, its shots rarely ever hit moving targets at range.

items.name: Hurricane, Dune
items.description: These weapons weren't even good in the first place, but then they got nerfed anyways. Artillery just kinda doesn't work in WR, it's either OP or useless.

items.name: Thermite, Vortex
items.description: Good luck hitting anything. No damage to make up for their horrid accuracy either.

items.name: Fainter
items.description: Was already bad and then got nerfed. Long reload and poor damage with shots that rarely hit moving targets.

items.name: Prisma
items.description: 48 second reload bro are we being serious right now? These weapons are technically fine at range but they are essentially one time use due to the absurdly long reload.

items.name: Ion
items.description: Outdated, poor damage. Since it only does about 5% less damage than its heavy counterpart (Zeus) despite being a medium weapon, it's one tier above.

items.name: Magnum, Taran
items.description: Outdated ancient plasma guns. Notably worse than Redeemer.

items.name: Thunder
items.description: Outdated ancient shotgun. Even at point blank range, Thunder loses to Avenger. That being said, Avenger costs gold and Thunder can be had for free, so you should use Thunder in the early game over Avenger.

items.name: Ballista, Arbalest
items.description: Outdated snipers with poor damage. Unlike trebuchet, they don’t deal massive single shot damage, and instead split their damage across several shots, so they are in a lower tier than it.

items.name: Noricum
items.description: Technically usable on builds like Dagon to counter immobile campers without exposing yourself, but it’s incredibly unreliable.

items.name: Chimera
items.description: A bad weapon, but a bit better than its medium and light counterparts.

items.name: Hydra, Spiral
items.description: Homing weapons always have lower damage to compensate for how they can deal damage without line of sight. Thus, one could imagine how 10+ year old homing weapons in the modern age barely even tickle.

items.name: Gekko
items.description: Super long range weapons generally have lower damage to compensate for how much range they have. Thus, one could imagine how a 10+ year old light laser weapon in the modern age tickles. Fun fact: This is the only weapon in the game whose projectile changes color based on its level.

items.name: Tulumbas, Pin
items.description: These used to be decent midrange burst weapons, often referred to as “RDB” or “Russian Death Button”. Nowadays, they are little more than a piece of WR history.

items.name: Orkan, Pinata
items.description: These used to be deadly close range burst weapons, often referred to as “DB” or “Deathbutton”. Nowadays, they are little more than a piece of WR history. Early game players should just stick to the Punisher family, as they cost silver while being moderately competitive options, though Pinata doesn’t cost gold and is thus an acceptable option in the extremely early game stages, where the burst it carries can actually cripple the enemy.

items.name: Molot T, Molot
items.description: The autocannon family unfortunately did not age nearly as well as the punisher family.

items.name: Aphid
items.description: Homing weapons always have lower damage to compensate for how they can deal damage without line of sight. Thus, one could imagine how 10+ year old homing weapons in the modern age barely even tickle.

items.name: Trident
items.description: A once deadly midrange weapon, now relegated to being an ancient part of WR history.

items.name: Nashorn
items.description: If you want midrange, use Kang Dae instead, as it has much better damage and a faster reload. The fact that Nashorn has 1100m and Kang Dae has 800m rarely ever matters.

items.name: Kang Dae
items.description: The prime midrange option for early game. It isn’t good, but it does the job for silver.

items.name: Ancile
items.description: Replacing a heavy weapon slot with an outdated bubble shield with poor durability and no usefulness against energy weapons is not a good idea.

items.name: Zeus
items.description: A slightly better Kang Dae that you shouldn’t waste your gold on.

items.name: Zenit
items.description: Technically usable on builds like Stryx with Lockdown Ammo to counter campers without exposing yourself, but it’s incredibly unreliable. Noricum is better for this very specific niche.

items.name: Trickster, Deceiver
items.description: Awful base damage with weak DoT means all these weapons do is charge enemy repair amplifiers for free.

items.name: Ecu
items.description: Doesn’t do damage, provides incredibly unreliable protection, takes a weapon slot, and gives enemies free nuclear amplifier charge.

items.name: Torch, Furnace
items.description: Trades the sustained DPS of Venire family for an extra 200m of range. Does pretty much the same burst DPS though.

items.name: Barq-a, Barq-b
items.description: Titan teslas with AoE damage that can ignore stealth and apply a powerful slowdown. Their damage isn’t the best, but their massive magazine makes up for it when used on brawlers that stay in the middle of the fight for a long time.

items.name: Venire, Vincere
items.description: These weapons are still the strongest midrangers in the game as of now, but not so much to the point where everything feels worse or clunky to use. Arbiter-equalizers are only a bit worse now.

items.name: UE Bulava, UE Kisten
items.description: Lethal homing rockets that are leaps and bounds stronger than their normal counterparts. Putting aside its obviously stronger stats for a moment, the UE variant of these weapons have their ancient aiming flaw almost entirely fixed, which makes them extremely versatile at chipping down & bursting down targets, and combining them with the Explosive Expert titan pilot skills makes them practically undodgeable. Even the mothership charge on these weapons is powerful. The only real downside of these weapons is that some awkward terrain of certain maps can make them harder to use, but otherwise a very small issue for the power delivered.

items.name: Evora, Veyron
items.description: The f2p standard brawling weapon, dealing incredibly high DPS and it's all grey damage. Their main limitation is that their damage is bad outside of point blank range.

items.name: Arbiter, Equalizer
items.description: Nerfed down f2p version of Venire family. Good performance past 300m, but noticeably weaker when enemies get close due to their range damage boosting mechanic. If you’ve never used them before, there’s a bit of a learning curve to understand their ideal firing mechanic (generally, try to stay at 30% heat when out of combat to max out the fire rate and make sure to never overheat).

items.name: ‼️UE Gendarme
items.description: Niche 800m weapon that is largely not worth investing in. Not bad or anything, but powercrept directly by the Furnace family. ‼️Specifically for builds running 4 or more Furnace/Torch family weapons, UE Gendarmes can often be comparable to adding more Furnaces due to the diminishing returns of the thermal breach effect.

items.name: ‼️Vendicatore
items.description: Most titans cannot justify using these weapons due to their insane 15 second downtime and unreliable projectile that's prone to missing fast moving enemies. Despite that, their burst damage is so high that they outrank many titan weapons anyways. ‼️For Eiffel and UE Ao Ming, Vendicatores in the summoned slots are often one of the best options, especially on ranged maps.

items.name: Fulger, Tonans
items.description: Technically viable for triggering deft on or even 100-to-0-ing glass cannon titans, but you will be bullied by normal robots if you equip a full set of them. On hybrid builds, Tonans is on par with Vendicatoire (better against titans, worse against bots).

items.name: Anguisher, Ruiner
items.description: Point blank burst shotguns; essentially worse Evora/Veyron.

items.name: Maha-Vajra, Vajra
items.description: Point blank burst shotguns; essentially worse Evora/Veyron.

items.name: Argon, Oxy
items.description: Rockets with decent effectiveness at a distance compared to most other close range titan weapons, but of course the sacrifice for that range is made in damage.

items.name: Huginn, Muninn
items.description: These weapons have an incredibly small mag, but they offer lockdown utility and better performance at range than most brawling titan weapons.

items.name: Chasm, Void
items.description: Trades much of the damage and the grey damage of Evora family for better range and accuracy. Okay at killing robots due to their smaller hitboxes, but overall a little clunky to use from their nerfed damage state.

items.name: UE Grom
items.description: Shotguns with unimpressive burst but insane sustain. Deal respectable chip damage at a distance when equipped with sharpshooter. Notable for their ability to instakill enemies before they can even trigger deft survivor due to how much damage each individual shot does, but the actual DPS is not that high due to the criminally slow fire rate.

items.name: Discordia, Tumultus
items.description: Downgraded Arbiter/Equalizer with bendy mechanics which can be... sorta useful?

items.name: Striker
items.description: I really tried to make this work, in theory it's a mini Vendicatore that never misses. But the damage is just too bad to replace Vendicatore for most circumstances.

items.name: Glaive, Lance
items.description: Focused damage into the last shot allows you to open up with a ton of burst damage. Surprisingly strong in practice when compared to how they sheet thanks to this feature, but they are still pretty dated and generally weaker versions of Arbiter/Equalizer.

items.name: Basilisk, Krait
items.description: Downgraded Arbiter/Equalizer.

items.name: Dazzler, Lantern
items.description: Damage from these weapons isn’t so good but has extremely fast mothership charge, cannot miss its shots, and also blind enemies.

items.name: Inferno, Pyro
items.description: Outdated flamethrowers with unremarkable damage but a flexible overheat system and decent splash.

items.name: ‼️UE Cyclone
items.description: Insanely expensive and outclassed by meta options. Still, not a bad weapon or anything, just incredibly mediocre for how much it costs to acquire and upgrade. ‼️The dedicated pilot for this weapon improves its performance considerably, but even then, it won’t be as good as most top meta weapons.

items.name: Gargantua, Pantagreul
items.description: Only usable in PvE. They literally get outdamaged by their drone counterpart.

items.name: Cataclysm, Cyclone
items.description: Decent damage at various ranges but they’re held back by their clunky lock on mechanic.

items.name: Grom, Squall
items.description: Point blank burst shotguns; essentially significantly worse Vajras.

items.name: UE Squall
items.description: Worse DPS than a normal squall while costing like 10x more to upgrade.

items.name: Kisten, Bulava
items.description: While their damage is incredibly high in theory, their accuracy is awful, so they rarely actually deal that damage except against slow or stationary targets.

items.name: Cinder
items.description: Only viable in PvE for the AoE damage. Incredibly outdated weapons in PvP.

items.name: Retaliator, Vengeance
items.description: Default machineguns. Use them if you have no better choice.

items.name: Gendarme, Curassier
items.description: No reason to buy these when the default machineguns are right there. More range, but bad damage and long reload.

items.name: Rupture, Tsar
items.description: Unlike the Gendarme family, these weapons don't even bring range to the table, there is seriously actually NO reason to get these, just use the default guns until you get something better.

[‼️] Items that can perform notably better when equipped with a specific build and go up on the tier list only when used that way.
[⬆️] Items that are normally low tier but have the potential to perform at a much higher tier than listed due to current meta circumstances.
[⬇️] Items that are normally high tier but will likely perform worse than usual at the moment due to current meta circumstances.
[👁️] Items so powerful that the meta is being bent around them. [⬆️] and [⬇️] tags are based on these.
